ranking.note: Security/privacy fixes rank above pure correctness fixes in this category, so the key-material leak moves ahead of the data-correctness P2s.
Still P2, but new-capability work is placed after the security and returned-data correctness P2s.
Raised to P2: restores the sendrawtransaction mempool-acceptance contract that downstream wallets rely on and is a stated prerequisite for wallet private broadcast; moved up accordingly.
Top of P3: assertion crash on authenticated malformed input plus JSON-RPC 2.0 spec compliance outranks the rest of the P3 bug tail.
Grouped with the other interface-machinery correctness fixes; empty 403 bodies break IPC clients outright.
Dropped RPC responses are lost returned data, which this category weights highest, so it leads the remaining P3 bugs.
Out-of-bounds read in the shared JSON parser is memory-safety hardening of the RPC front door; ranked with the machinery fixes.
Same defect class as the P2 false-success fixes (#35837, #36343), so it leads the P3 bug group even though invalidateblock is an admin tool.
Batch reply IDs are returned-data correctness for every batch client, which this category ranks first; its solo score underweighted that.
Unrelated key metadata injected into shared PSBTs is a privacy leak, grouped with the other key-exposure fixes.
Kept P3: the pruning/index behaviour belongs to its own area; only the error payloads are rpc surface.
Silent misrouting of trailing -rpcwallet is a real cli bug but affects fewer callers than the server-side correctness fixes above it.
Miners using longpoll currently get a spurious 'Internal bug detected' on shutdown; that is a user-visible wrong RPC error, higher than its solo score.
Hidden warnings matter, but -getinfo is a display convenience rather than a programmatic contract, so it sits below the server-side fixes.
Defense-in-depth against thread stalls on the HTTP server belongs with the other interface-hardening fixes rather than in the tail.
setban silently discarding bans while reporting success is a wrong-result bug, grouped with the other such fixes.
Warning about silent key cloning touches address-reuse risk, so it ranks with the diagnostics-correctness group rather than the tail.
Useful privacy control, but it is a new mode on an existing argument rather than a defect; placed after the bug group.
Clear feature gap with a linked request, but additive output for tooling ranks below the correctness fixes above it.
Misleading analyzepsbt output is the same class as the other wrong-result fixes, so it rises out of the tail.
Contradictory network labels across getaddrmaninfo and getnodeaddresses mislead clients filtering by network; higher than its solo score.
addnode remove/getaddednodeinfo rejecting equivalent addresses is a user-visible RPC matching bug, grouped with the other fixes.
Cross-RPC progress inconsistency is real but narrow; placed at the end of the bug group.
Admin logging ergonomics with a changed return schema ranks below the returned-data and security fixes; also competes with #35387.
REST/RPC parity gap with a named consumer, but additive; grouped with the other interface-gap features.
Optional unit formatting is convenience for callers that can already convert; grouped with the additive features.
Aggregate traffic stats are additive monitoring data with one linked issue; ranks with the other new-field features, not above the bug tail.
Deprecation discipline matters here, so it leads the consistency group together with #36785.
Breaking removal of an RPC needs a direction decision, but assumeutxo loading is still experimental; placed with the other interface-shape changes.
Interface plumbing for GUI snapshot loading; its value depends on the unresolved #36778 direction.
Better diagnostics only; ranked below the gaps that force callers into workarounds.
Pairs with #36488 as the same camelCase-to-snake_case cleanup, so it sits next to it rather than at the bottom.
Test-harness convenience for regtest only; below the features that serve production callers.
New diagnostic field with no external consumer asking; this category ranks such additions low.
Explicit RFC for a speculative scheduling feature with in-memory-only state; bottom of P3.
Its rpc surface is a single trigger method; the substance is a P2P protocol change, so it ranks last in this category.
Lowered to P4: test-only coverage of one decode path, narrow and nothing depends on it, consistent with the other marginal entries.

inconsistencies: #34038 and #35387 solve the same problem (making trace logging usable and controllable at runtime) in competing ways; reviewers should settle on one. Review #34038 first since #35355 is built on top of it, then close or rebase the other.

#36778 (replace loadtxoutset RPC with a startup argument) directly contradicts #33117 (expose loadtxoutset through interfaces for GUI/IPC clients) and partly #35054 (adds a downloadutxoset RPC). The #36778 direction decision should be taken before reviewing #33117 in detail.

#35837, #36343 and #36555 are the same defect class: an RPC reporting success/completion when the operation did not fully succeed. #35837 and #36343 are P2 because wallet and indexer callers act on the result; #36555 stays P3 only because invalidateblock is an administrative tool. Worth reviewing as a group for a consistent error-reporting rule.
#36503 and #36266 both harden dumptxoutset rollback handling and touch the same path; review #36503 first (it removes an outright crash) to avoid rework in #36266.

#36200, #36204, #36745 and #36187 all touch HTTP server connection/bind handling; they are independent problems but overlapping code, so merging #36187 and then the two DoS fixes in one pass avoids repeated conflict resolution.
#36488 and #36785 are two halves of the same camelCase/snake_case option cleanup for wallet RPC options; review them together so the alias and deprecation policy match.

#36648, #36332 and #35370 all concern key material leaking through descriptor/PSBT RPC paths (error echoes, unrelated MuSig2 metadata, un-strippable key origins). A single reviewer pass would produce a more coherent policy than three separate ones.
result.notes: The category has a clear top: one P1 local-credential-exposure fix and a cluster of HTTP-server security/DoS and returned-data correctness fixes. Below that sits a long P3 tail that I ordered by the category's own priorities (correctness of what callers get back, then interface security hardening, then gaps with evidence of demand, then consistency/documentation), which moves several interface-machinery bug fixes up and several additive new-field features down relative to their solo scores. Only two band changes were needed: #36566 up to P2 and #36626 down to P4.
